dedupe_keys.name: g cat gnss coverage analysis tool for constellation design

description: The GNSS Coverage Analysis Tool (G-CAT) is a software suite described in a paper on system-level preliminary performance analysis and design of global navigation satellite system constellations. It takes the state vector of each satellite as input and provides constellation coverage performance; the tool includes an orbit propagator, an attitude propagator, an algorithm that identifies the visibility region on the Earth's surface from each satellite and a counter that computes how many satellites are in view from given locations. The analysis accounts both for coverage requirements and for the robustness of the constellation to transient or catastrophic failures, and Galileo is used as the reference case. Because of its low computational burden it can be used to compute the optimal number of satellites per orbital plane, assuming uniform in-plane spacing, that meets coverage and accuracy requirements. Producer: the authors named above, in a 19-page open-access article (21 figures) published in the International Review of Aerospace Engineering, June 2020. Coverage: generic constellations, demonstrated on Galileo. Access: the article on arXiv; the abstract page does not offer the code, so availability must be confirmed with the authors. Licence and cost: free to read, tool licence not stated for the model code; the describing arXiv preprint is under the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: coverage and geometry only, with no signal, ionosphere or receiver modelling. Simulation uses: satellite-outage and availability studies of navigation constellations. Related record: the live Galileo constellation status (data-galileo-constellation-status).
